data.bug_class: uninitialized output pointer on error path (invalid free / free of non-heap pointer)
data.rationale: Reachability: LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput (format_command_fuzzer.c:51) passes an attacker-controlled string as the printf-style format to redisFormatCommand. When the format contains '%' followed by a non-ASCII/invalid specifier (e.g. byte 0xe0), the default printf-detection branch in redisvFormatCommand fails all size-prefix checks (lines 411-460) and falls through to fmt_invalid (line 462), jumping to format_err and then cleanup (lines 529-547). The cleanup block frees temporaries and returns error_type without ever assigning *target. redisFormatCommand (line 562) likewise never sets *target on failure. The caller in the fuzz harness declares 'char *cmd' uninitialized and calls hi_free(cmd) whenever cmd != NULL, so it frees a garbage stack value -> 'free(): invalid pointer' abort, reproduced deterministically with input 'x%\xe0\x80d'. Root cause is the missing '*target = NULL' initialization on the error/cleanup paths of redisvFormatCommand: an error return leaves the output parameter unwritten, violating the API contract and turning uninitialized memory into an invalid free. Fix: set *target = NULL in the cleanup path (and/or at function entry) of redisvFormatCommand.
